title: prevent-sse-overlap-reassembly-windows-and-emit-boundary-markers
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Fixes SSE streaming fragment reassembly where overlapping TCP/SSE payloads could cause partial JSON truncation and out-of-order event emission for the OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Adds reassembly windowing and explicit boundary markers to make downstream parsers deterministic. No breaking API changes.
body: Summary: This PR fixes two classes of bugs in the OpenAI-compat SSE path: (1) overlapping TCP/SSE payloads that produced partial/truncated JSON objects when fragments were coalesced incorrectly, and (2) event reordering when multiple small events arrived in a single wire chunk without clear boundaries. The fix introduces a compact, optional 'chunk_seq' marker in SSE data frames for reassembly ordering and a bounded reassembly window to avoid unbounded buffer growth. It also emits a lightweight 'boundary' sentinel when a logical event ends so downstream OpenAI-compatible clients (and our internal parsers) can deterministically split events even in the face of sticky framing.
commits:
- 8 commits
  - a1f3d2a: add reassembly window and chunk_seq metadata to SSE encoder
  - b47c9d1: implement ordered reassembler with gap-tolerance and timeouts
  - c592d4f: emit boundary sentinel when event end detected
  - d10a8b3: normalize newline handling and tighten parser state machine
  - e7b2f4c: add unit tests for split-join scenarios and size-limited windows
  - f112a7b: integration fixture to reproduce customer SUP-5891 case
  - f9c88de: docs: explain chunk_seq and boundary markers for compatibility consumers
  - 1a3be58: minor telemetry (metric: sse.reassembly.gaps) and logging improvements
files_changed:
8 files changed at a high level:
  - openai_compat/streaming/encoder.py (writes optional chunk metadata and boundary sentinel)
  - openai_compat/streaming/reassembler.go (core reassembly algorithm, windowing, timeouts)
  - openai_compat/streaming/parser.rs (parser tweaks: normalized CRLF handling)
  - tests/streaming/test_fragmentation.py (unit tests for fragment reorder and truncation)
  - integration/compat/fixtures/sse_replay_fixture.json (replay trace from SUP-5891)
  - docs/openai_compat/streaming.md (compat notes for clients)
  - ci/flake-repro/Makefile (helper for deterministic TCP split tests)
  - telemetry/metrics.yaml (adds sse.reassembly.gaps metric)
review_conversation:
Luis Ortega: Please justify adding chunk_seq since it slightly changes the wire format. Are we sure clients won't depend on strictly raw 'data: ' semantics?
Maya Chen: Chunk_seq is optional and only included for events flagged as potentially split (heuristic: payload > 1KB or encoder detects previous partial buffer). The parser ignores unknown fields so backward compatibility is preserved.
Priya Raman: Reassembler.go looks complex; can we add more unit tests around gap behavior?
Maya Chen: Added explicit tests for large gaps and for sequence resets; also added telemetry so we can monitor real-world gap rates before rolling out wider.
Tomás Alvarez: CI failed on the first run due to a test harness race in test_fragmentation; I requested a rerun.
Maya Chen: Fixed the race by adding a deterministic flush hook in the fixture; reran CI.
Luis Ortega: Approving, but add a short blurb to docs about how older clients will see no change unless they opt-in.
Maya Chen: Added docs blurb. Approved-by: Luis Ortega, Priya Raman. Merge-ready.
ci_summary:
CI timeline:
  - initial run: 9/84 tests failed (flaky test_fixture timing)
  - rerun after race fix: all checks passed (unit, integration, lint)
  - canary performance: added a microbenchmark that shows <2% median latency impact for typical small-message workloads; larger messages benefit from fewer re-parses.
  - status: pass
testing_and_qa: Unit tests added for fragmentation/reassembly, integration fixture reproduces customer trace SUP-5891. Manual QA: streamed several long function-call examples + embedded JSON blocks from curl and from our internal openai-compat client; verified no truncated JSON and consistent function-call sentinel ordering. Load test: synthetic 10k concurrent streams showed negligible throughput regression; memory growth bounded by configured window. Metrics: implemented sse.reassembly.gaps to surface gap events for 2-week canary.
backward_compatibility_notes: The chunk_seq and boundary markers are optional and parsers skip unknown fields. Existing clients that split on blank lines will continue to work in the common case. Clients who require strict byte-level interpretation can set a compatibility flag on the API to disable chunk metadata — this PR leaves that flag in place and disabled by default.
merge_details: Merged via squash (squash-merge). Commit message: 'fix(streaming): deterministic SSE reassembly with optional chunk_seq and boundary sentinel (fixes SUP-5891, ENG-2437)'. Backported patch to release/1.12.x as cherrypick 39210-cp for enterprise customers. Deployed to staging the same day and rolled to canary with metrics monitoring enabled.
notes: Follow-ups: - Consider exposing reassembly window config to Dedicated customers in Console. - Evaluate switching from inline JSON chunk metadata to binary boundary markers if we see significant client-side noise. - Keep sse.reassembly.gaps on for at least 2 weeks to ensure no regressions.
